memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "All the other articles used in the service of the tabernacle, whatever their function, including all the tent pegs for it and those for the courtyard, are to be bronze." - Exodus 27:19 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God's instructions reach all the way down to the tent pegs. Not the ark, not the golden lampstand — the pegs, driven into the dirt, holding ropes taut. God specified those too. "Whatever their function," the verse says, as if to make sure nothing is left out.

Sit with that for a moment. The tent pegs were the humblest items in the entire tabernacle. Buried in the ground, unseen, unremarkable, and entirely essential. Without them the whole structure would collapse in the first strong wind. Yet God named them and gave them their material, just as He did the mercy seat.

This is enormously encouraging for anyone who feels like a tent peg. Perhaps your role is hidden, your work unnoticed, your contribution small in others' eyes. God does not overlook it. Jesus said that even a cup of cold water given in His name does not lose its reward (Matt 10:42). In God's house there is no such thing as an unimportant part. The pegs held the whole thing steady, and God knew exactly what they were made of. He knows what you are made of too, and He has placed you deliberately.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
Do I feel my role is too small or hidden to matter to God?
Who around me is doing "tent peg" work that I should notice and value?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, You named even the tent pegs. Thank You that nothing done for You is too small to matter. Help me serve faithfully in hidden places, knowing You see and value it. Amen.
